newsitem.title: SPAIN: Canal Satelite files suits against Spain with EU.
newsitem.headline: Canal Satelite files suits against Spain with EU.

text.p: Spanish digital television group Canal Satelite said it filed two complaints on Friday against Spain with the European Union's Competition Commission.

The company said it was taking legal action after the Spanish government adopted norms last Friday that helped a government-backed operator, but made it difficult for Canal Satelite to enter in the satellite digital television market.

Canal Satelite, which is a digital platform initiative comprising communications group Prisa, Canal Plus via its Sogecable holding, and TV station Antena 3, said it also objected to public aid being offered to its competitors.

"It (the aid) has allowed them to participate as shareholders in the digital television operator under the auspices of the government that will compete with Canal Satelite Digital without this having been justified by the notion of public service," the company said in a statement.
The Spanish cabinet approved a new satellite television norm last Friday stipulating that decoders have to be compatible with various digital platforms.
Canal Satelite, which launched Spain's first digital platform last Thursday, has ordered decoders for the project that will not meet the new standards.
But when the new regulation was announced, Spain's Development Minister said it met European Union requirements.
A universal decoder allows viewers to tune into all platforms available with the same equipment.

Canal Satelite will compete with the operators of the second digital platform, a group comprised of Telefonica, Radio and Television of Spain (RTVE), Mexican group Televisa and several regional television channels.
